title: International Environmental Law and the Governance of Planetary Risk
seo_title: International Environmental Law and the Governance of Planetary Risk
excerpt: International environmental law governs how states, institutions, and courts respond to ecological harm that crosses borders, threatens common resources, or endangers planetary systems. This article explains transboundary harm, prevention, precaution, due diligence, environmental impact assessment, cooperation, public participation, biodiversity protection, climate obligations, marine environmental protection, hazardous waste control, pollution prevention, human rights, corporate responsibility, and environmental rule of law. It examines Stockholm, Rio, the Convention on Biological Diversity, UNFCCC, Paris Agreement, Espoo Convention, Aarhus Convention, Basel Convention, climate advisory opinions, and emerging planetary-risk governance. The article also addresses scientific uncertainty, cumulative harm, irreversible damage, capacity inequality, Global South claims, and institutional fragmentation. By connecting doctrine, institutions, case studies, and lawyer-facing workflows, it shows how international environmental law transforms ecological risk into legal responsibility while exposing enforcement gaps, political conflict, and the limits of treaty-based environmental cooperation.
